title: Do not treat a memory as retrievable real advice when its evidence_refs point at a file under tests/
trigger: when reviewing pending or active memories in this project's own DD store during an audit, or when writing/running a test that seeds memories through proposeMemory/putAtom for evaluation purposes
behavior_delta: Do not treat a memory as real advice when its evidence_refs point at a file under tests/ and its why mentions 'eval fixture' or 'safe to delete'. That combination is a strong signal it is leftover test content mistakenly promoted into a real project's live store. Reject or flag it for deletion in the audit UI instead. A full audit of this project's own store (2026-09-19) found 10 such memories sitting `active` under project_id 'supermem' with content copied from tests/engine/health/abstention-eval.test.js, several already delivered as real advisory context in real sessions (activation_count > 0). The eval harness's own fixtures (src/eval/replay.js's evaluationStore()) are correctly isolated in a separate temp store under project_id 'eval' and never touch a real project's store — the contamination found came from fixture content copied into the real store some other way (manual proposal or exploratory testing), not a bug in the eval harness itself.
